questions.question: Which of the following does not provide articulations to ribs?

suspectLines.text: The spinous processes of vertebrae do not provide articulations to the ribs. The source notes that the two facets on the head of a typical rib are separated by a transverse crest that attaches to the intervertebral disc above it.

questions.question: Which among the following is incorrect regarding Sibson's fascia?

options.text: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib

suspectLines.text: The incorrect statement is that Sibson's fascia attaches to the inner border of the second rib. The source describes Sibson's fascia (suprapleural membrane) as a fascial plane separating lower neck and thorax, covering the lung apex and attaching to the inner border of the first rib and posteriorly to the anterior border of the transverse process of C7. It is strengthened by fibers derived from scalenus minimus, and the subclavian vessels lie on top of it.

questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Sibson's fascia attaches to the inner border of the second rib. The source describes Sibson's fascia (suprapleural membrane) as a fascial plane separating lower neck and thorax, covering the lung apex and attaching to the inner border of the first rib and posteriorly to the anterior border of the transverse process of C7. It is strengthened by fibers derived from scalenus minimus, and the subclavian vessels lie on top of it.

questions.question: On the ides of March, Julius Caesar was stabbed 23 times. One such stab wound was present in the left supraclavicular fossa, piercing his left lung. Which of the following provides the vertebral attachment of the fascia present here?

suspectLines.text: The stabbed lung apex is covered by Sibson's fascia (suprapleural membrane). The source states that its vertebral attachment is posteriorly to the anterior border of the transverse process of the C7 vertebra; anteriorly it attaches to the inner border of the first rib.
